chunks: And it was said to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام: “Indeed, the people narrate from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله that he said:”
“Indeed, charity is not permissible for a wealthy person, nor for one possessing strength and soundness.”
So he عليه السلام said: “He did say, ‘for a wealthy person,’ but he did not say, ‘for one possessing strength and soundness.’”

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةَ: charity; financial giving discussed here as a legal entitlement
key_terms.لَا تَحِلُّ: is not permissible; denotes legal prohibition or invalid entitlement
key_terms.لِذِي مِرَّةٍ سَوِيٍّ: for one possessing strength and sound condition; the disputed phrase in the report
key_terms.لِغَنِيٍّ: for a wealthy person; one who is financially well-off and not eligible
key_terms.يَرْوُونَ: they narrate; indicates transmission of a reported prophetic statement

ai.seo_question: Is charity forbidden for a strong and able-bodied person in this hadith from Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal point concerning who may receive charity. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rejects the addition that charity is forbidden for every strong and able-bodied person, affirming only the restriction concerning the wealthy. The report is significant in clarifying the precise wording of a prophetic tradition used in financial law.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3671 - It was said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as):
"People narrate from the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) that he said:
'Charity is not permissible for a wealthy person nor for one who is strong and able-bodied.'"
Imam (as) replied: "He (sw) indeed said it is not permissible for a wealthy person, but he (sw) did not say for one who is strong and able-bodied."
